newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: North Korea threatens action over submarine deaths.
newsitem.headline: North Korea threatens action over submarine deaths.

text.p: North Korea threatened "serious consequences" on Wednesday over the deaths of its soldiers who came ashore in South Korea from a submarine two weeks ago, the U.S.-led United Nations Command said.
The threat was made by North Korean military officers during a border meeting with representatives of the command, which oversees a ceasefire that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
The representatives of the Korean People's Army again demanded the return of the submarine and the crew during the meeting in the border crossing village of Panmunjom, a U.N. Command statement said.

"At the end of the meeting, the senior representative of the KPA delegation indicated that serious consequences, which would be announced, would occur as a result of the deaths of their soldiers," it said.
Of an estimated 26 North Koreans that landed on an east coast beach, 22 have been shot and killed by South Korean troops or found dead. One has been captured alive.
During the meeting, North Korea again maintained the submarine accidentally drifted into South Korean waters, the statement said. North Korea has previously threatened retaliation over the incident.
